top_choice_rationale: The optical lattice clock rests on a distinct principle, magic-wavelength trapping of many neutral atoms, that is separate from the 2005 comb and 2012 single-ion prizes. It has been reproduced independently at the 1e-18 level by several laboratories, so the systematics are tested and understood. The allocation to Katori and Ye is the cleanest on the list, since all eight members proposed the same two names, and the citation can be worded narrowly on the principle without relying on the redefinition of the second. P002 is a respectable second: a clear theory-to-experiment chain, but with unsettled pairing physics and a contestable third name with Cao and independent groups left outside. A prize is preferable to none.
recusal_note: Long-time close collaborator of Anne L'Huillier (2023 laureate) and co-author with Lund and Keller attosecond groups; no apparent connection to Katori, Ye, or the P002 candidates. Atomic physics is my own field, a bias to declare rather than a recusal ground.
